text:
Happy Saturday evening! We've had a gorgeous run of sunshine, and it should hold right through sunset, which comes at 5:53 under a clear sky. It's still in the upper 50s now, but once the sun drops, the temperature goes with it. I'd grab a jacket for any sunset walk.

Tonight stays clear and quiet, with a low around 35 in the city. Outlying spots will be colder, and the forecasters expect another round of fairly heavy frost by morning. If you park outside, plan a few extra minutes to scrape the windshield, and bring in anything tender.

Tomorrow is a near repeat: full sunshine, a high near 61, and a light south breeze picking up later in the day. The models run from the upper 50s to the mid 60s, and I'd bet on low 60s. It's a great day to get outside. Sunday night stays milder, in the low 40s.

A cold front arrives Monday with more clouds, maybe a sprinkle, then Tuesday turns much cooler, in the 40s.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-24T18:26:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Dry weather to persist into early next week, with minimal chances of light rain with a frontal passage on Monday.
  2. High pressure continues through mid to late next week with little to no rain in the forecast.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 225 PM EDT Saturday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A beautiful start to the weekend so far today with high pressure positioned over the region. The clear skies, light winds, and seasonable temperatures will continue through tonight. Expect another round of fairly heavy frost by Sunday morning, with lows in the low 20s to low 30s. Tomorrow will be a near repeat of today, though south flow will increase a bit later in the day as the ridge axis shifts east of the region. Relative humidity values will once again drop to around 30% tomorrow afternoon, and highs will be a little warmer than today, mainly in the low to mid 60s. The south flow will continue Sunday night ahead of a cold front, helping to keep temperatures quite a bit warmer than the past couple of nights, especially in the Champlain/St Lawrence Valleys. The front will push southward out of Canada and through our area on Monday, bringing mainly increasing clouds as it does so. A few light rain showers can't be ruled out, mainly over the higher terrain in the northern mountains. However, given recent trends and the very dry antecedent airmass, expect most areas will see only sprinkles, if anything. Winds will turn to the northwest behind the front, ushering in another cool and dry airmass. We'll see a return to much cooler temperatures; Tuesday will likely only get into the 40s to low 50s in most areas after morning lows in the 20s to around 30F. KEY MESSAGE 2: A strong area of high pressure will build in overhead early Wednesday behind our Tuesday cold front helping to extend our dry period for many. Southerly flow associated with the high will also help to rebound our temperatures into the late week with highs warming from the the low to mid 50s Wednesday to the upper 50s to mid 60s by Friday. There is another chance for a weak frontal passage late week, but it looks rather unimpressive and unable to break us from this dry pattern. Of note in the ensemblistic guidance, both the GEFS and euro ensembles show only a 30-40% chance for a cumulative inch of rain through the first week of November. While the prolonged stretch of dry weather will continue with some days of low relative humidity values next week, prevailing wind conditions look too light to note any serious fire weather concerns right now. That said, channeled southerly flow Thursday afternoon could see trends towards marginal critical winds with gusts in the forecast between 20 to 25 MPH. It is still to far out to say with any certainty, but Thursday winds will need to be monitored going forward for any fire weather concerns.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The continued dry but pleasant weather will continue over the weekend. It was a cold morning with temperatures in the 20s, but the afternoon will be sunny and warmer with highs in the 50s. A few spots could hit 60 degrees. Sunday will continue the sunny skies with pleasant highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The fall foliage is now past peak throughout the region, but some trees still have color, so the weekend will be great for viewing any remaining foliage. Overall, the week will remain dry, but the fire danger will remain relatively low due to a lack of wind. A cold front will come through on Monday. An isolated shower is possible, but most of the region is expected to remain dry. Highs will be in the 50s to around 60 degrees. The front will, however, usher in colder air for Tuesday. Despite mostly sunny skies, it will be chilly with highs in the 40s. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are expected. Wednesday and Thursday will be mostly sunny. Highs will be near 50 degrees on Wednesday, but Thursday’s highs will be closer to 60 degrees. Another system may bring a higher chance for showers on Friday, but no significant rain is in the forecast.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-24T11:50:00Z — same caveat): Lots of sunshine, turning a bit milder Saturday — After a widespread hard freeze, expect a nice temperature rebound through Saturday. Highs reach the 50s to near 60. Besides a few morning clouds and patchy fog, expect nearly full sunshine. Tonight will again be quite cold, due to clear skies and light wind. Temperatures fall back to the 20s and low 30s. Expect another round of frost and freeze conditions. High pressure stays nearby Sunday, bringing full sunshine! It turns warmer, thanks to a light south breeze that develops. Highs reach the mid-60s. An approaching cold front brings more clouds and a few spot showers for northern areas on Monday. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall. Highs will be near 60. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mix of sun and clouds. Wednesday stays cool, with highs near 50 and a partly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs near 60, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely later Thursday into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with partly sunny skies. Highs reach the mid and upper 50s.
